# Artifact Evaluation for "AMG: AMX–GPU Cooperative Acceleration of Billion-Scale ANNS via GEMM Reformulation"

In this artifact, we provide guidelines for reproducing the key experimental
results presented in the paper. The experiments fall into three main
categories:

1. **End-to-end performance (Fig. 11)** — End-to-end performance (QPS)
   comparison for IVF-CPU, IVF-UVM, IVF-UVM+QG, RUMMY, RUMMY+QG, and AMG on
   DEEP1B, SIFT1B, and TEXT1B under different configurations. For clarity,
   each plot annotates the lowest QPS value.
2. **Ablation study (Fig. 12)** — Performance ablation study of AMG on SIFT1B.
   QPS is normalized to IVF-CPU.
3. **Throughput comparison (Fig. 19)** — Throughput comparison between RUMMY
   and AMG under different interconnect settings.

## Prerequisites

- The H100 (GNR) machine, with the GPU reserved and visible (`nvidia-smi`
  must succeed).
- Prebuilt billion-scale indexes and datasets on shared storage
  (`/fast-lab-share/mhkim/anns_index/`).
- Build tools: `g++-13`, `g++-10`, CUDA 12.9, Intel oneAPI (MKL), Gurobi 12.

## One-time build

This repo bundles four modified faiss forks as source:

| Directory | Base | Used by |
|---|---|---|
| `cabana/` | faiss 1.11.0, g++-13 | Fig. 11, Fig. 12 (AMG, IVF-CPU, IVF-UVM+QG) |
| `rummy/` | faiss 1.6.4, g++-10 | Fig. 11 (RUMMY) |
| `uvm/` | faiss 1.6.4, g++-10 | Fig. 11 (IVF-UVM) |
| `updated_cabana/` | faiss 1.11.0, g++-13 | Fig. 19 (throughput\_comparison) |
| `end_to_end/rummy_qg/` | faiss 1.6.4, g++-10 | Fig. 11 (RUMMY+QG) |

Each fork is built from source on first run (~30–60 min per fork). Subsequent
runs skip the faiss build if `<fork>/build/faiss/libfaiss.a` already exists.

**GPU architecture**: all `do_cmake.sh` files default to `gpu=80` (A100).
Change to `gpu=90` for H100 before the first build:

```bash
sed -i 's/^gpu=80/gpu=90/' cabana/do_cmake.sh rummy/do_cmake.sh uvm/do_cmake.sh \
    updated_cabana/do_cmake.sh end_to_end/rummy_qg/do_cmake.sh
```

Then build everything:

```bash
cd /home/mhkim/MICRO-2026-AMG
./build_all.sh          # builds all faiss forks + eval binaries (~2–4 h first run)
./throughput_comparison/build.sh   # builds amg_pcie_emulation (Fig. 19)
```

## Running experiments for Figure 11, Figure 12, and Figure 19

All run scripts are resumable: finished logs in each `results/` directory are
skipped on re-invocation (`FORCE=1 ./run_all.sh` re-runs everything), and
`./run_all.sh plot` only (re)generates the figure from existing results.

### Figure 11 — End-to-end performance (`end_to_end/`)

```bash
cd end_to_end
./run_all.sh
```

Runs all systems on DEEP1B, SIFT1B, and TEXT1B, then produces
`end_to_end/end_to_end.pdf` (and `.png`). Note: IVF-UVM and RUMMY build their
1B indexes in-process (several hours per dataset), so the full campaign takes
about a day; AMG loads the cached index from shared storage.

### Figure 12 — Ablation study (`ablation_study/`)

```bash
cd ablation_study
./run_all.sh
```

Runs the six ablation stages on SIFT1B (topk=10, nprobe=32) — IVF-CPU
(AVX512), +QG (AVX512), +QG (AMX), +Sched. (AMX+GPU), +GPU Pipelining, and
+GPU Caching — then produces `ablation_study/ablation_study.pdf` (and `.png`).

### Figure 19 — Throughput comparison (`throughput_comparison/`)

```bash
cd throughput_comparison
./run_all.sh
```

Runs AMG on TEXT1B under emulated PCIe 6.0, PCIe 7.0, and NVLink 5.0
interconnects, then produces `throughput_comparison/throughput_comparison.pdf`
(and `.png`). The RUMMY bars are derived from the Figure 11 result
(`end_to_end/results/e2e_rummy_text.txt`), so run the Figure 11 experiment
first.
